comparison: Both evaluate the core experimental finding of within-module grid cell variability (C16, C17, C25, C29-C34, C41, C42). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED and convincing. OpenEval emphasizes the methodological soundness of within- vs. between-cell comparisons and statistical tests, while peer reviewers highlight the systematic and convincing nature of the statistical analysis and control analyses. High agreement on this central finding.

Both evaluate the theoretical framework about translational invariance and why variability matters (C12, C13, C14). Both find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the logical framework and mathematical soundness with Figure 1 support, while peer reviewers accept the hypothesis as well-stated and clear. Complete agreement on theoretical motivation.

Both evaluate RNN modeling results showing that models reproduce observed variability (C18, C19, C39, C40, C66, C67). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes modest sample size (three networks per condition) as a limitation, while peer reviewers do not raise concerns and view it as supporting biological relevance. Agreement on support despite OpenEval noting methodological limitation.

Both evaluate functional benefits of variability through decoding analysis (C20, C43-C47). Both find evidence SUPPORTED and convincing. OpenEval notes methodological soundness but limitations to linear decoding and Poisson noise assumptions. Peer reviewers emphasize the convincing and important nature of enhanced decoding evidence. OpenEval also evaluates modeling assumptions (C55-C58) which peer reviewers address separately in R5. Strong agreement on functional significance.

Both evaluate methodological assumptions in the decoding analysis (C55, C56, C57, C58). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes validation against real data strengthens the evaluation, while peer reviewers find the systematic approach convincing with no concerns about assumptions. Agreement on methodological validity.

Both touch on the inference that individual modules encode more information (C50). OpenEval evaluates C48-C50 as SUPPORTED but notes C50 is computational demonstration rather than direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers include C50 in their evaluation of the decoding analysis and find it convincing. Slight difference in emphasis: OpenEval more cautious about inferential nature, peer reviewers more accepting.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about grid cells and prior knowledge (C1-C11) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, likely because reviewers focus on novel findings rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates analogy to visual cortex (C51, C52) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, suggesting reviewers did not focus on this speculative analogy.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of study limitations regarding conservative inclusion criteria (C53, C54) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this limitation is appropriately acknowledged by authors.

OpenEval evaluates discussion of continuous attractor models (C59-C64) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment that findings don't directly challenge these models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this discussion point.

OpenEval evaluates hypothesis about mechanistic origin via network defects (C65, C68) as UNCERTAIN, noting it remains speculative despite RNN support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval evaluates alternative hypothesis about place-to-grid cell models (C69-C74) as UNCERTAIN, noting logical reasoning but speculative nature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this alternative mechanism discussion.

OpenEval evaluates summary of prior findings about grid-hippocampus interactions (C75-C77) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are established prior work rather than novel claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological descriptions from public dataset (C78-C81) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are straightforward methodological descriptions from cited work.
